text:
Marissa Cole: Trying to lock beta scope + target customers + GA criteria for Shadow Evals this week. Want alignment across Console/Telemetry/Security so we don’t ship ourselves into a corner. Dropping strawman below.

Marissa Cole: Beta scope (MVP):
- Per-route shadowing: sample % + allowlist (customer/org) + region (optional)
- 1 shadow target per route (model/version + optional quant/profile)
- Async execution, never blocks primary
- Metrics: latency/cost deltas + judge win-rate + format adherence (basic)
- Console dashboard: time series + breakdown by route/model/region + compare primary vs shadow
- Guardrails: kill switch, capacity budget, tag allowlist

Marissa Cole: Beta customers: 2–3 design partners (enterprise) + 1 internal dogfood route. 

Marissa Cole: GA criteria (draft):
- Proven no primary p99 regression beyond budget
- Security: retention/redaction defaults, access controls, customer opt-out
- SRE: alerts + runbook validated
- Telemetry: stable schema + cardinality limits
- Rollouts: policy gates can reference judge win-rate thresholds

Marissa Cole: Can folks sanity check what’s missing / what’s too big?

Paula Mendes: +1. Main thing from rollouts side: beta should ship with “quality gate read-only” vs “enforced rollback”?

Paula Mendes: I’m worried we’ll end up auto-holding canaries based on noisy judge metrics before we have calibration. Could we do: beta = gates visible + alerting only; GA = gates allowed to block/rollback?

Dylan Brooks: From Console/Tooling: supporting 1 target per route makes UI much simpler. Multi-target comparisons can wait. Agree.

Dylan Brooks: Would also suggest in beta we only support:
- route filter
- time window
- primary model + shadow model
And defer “slice by prompt template / customer_id” etc. That’s where cardinality bites.

Logan Wright: Telemetry: strongly recommend we *do not* expose raw per-request diffs in beta (or at least not as a default). Aggregates first.

Logan Wright: For schema stability, we can commit to:
- `shadow_eval.run_started`
- `shadow_eval.run_completed`
- `shadow_eval.score_*`
but the dimensions need to be locked early (route_id, primary_model_id, shadow_model_id, region, sampling_policy_id). Anything else should be “debug logs” gated.

Chloe Martin: Console backend POV: if we’re committing to comparisons, we need to decide join key now (request_id or something). Otherwise dashboard queries get gnarly.

Chloe Martin: Also: we should define what happens if shadow run times out / is dropped due to budget. Do we count as error? separate “dropped” series?

Talia Benson: Program note: we’re ~10-12 weeks end-to-end if we keep scope tight. If we add multi-target + enforced rollback in beta, schedule blows up.

Naomi Feldman: Security/Compliance: beta scope is fine *if* we hard-gate storage:
- default retention short (e.g., 7 days) and configurable down to 0
- redaction on by default for prompts/outputs (PII filters + allowlist overrides)
- no customer content in non-prod (no “copy to dev for debugging”)

Naomi Feldman: Also need explicit customer-facing language: shadowing does not impact end-user response, but it *does* execute model with their data, so we need opt-in + DPA alignment.

Alicia Perez: UX: for beta, we should avoid calling it “A/B” in Console. Customers will assume response changes. Suggest “Shadow Evals (non-impacting)” + tooltip copy.

Kenji Nakamura: +1. Also in rollouts UI, this should look like a “preflight” panel rather than a canary stage.

Marissa Cole: On Paula’s point: I’m aligned with “read-only gates” for beta. GA can enable “enforced gates” once we have reliability + calibration guidance.

Paula Mendes: Great. So beta = dashboard + alert thresholds; GA = policy engine can hold/rollback.

Logan Wright: Re: dropped vs error: pls separate.
- dropped_due_to_budget
- dropped_due_to_backpressure
- shadow_timeout
- shadow_exec_error
We don’t want “shadow failing” to page like prod traffic failing.

Chloe Martin: +1. Console needs clear labeling too (“shadow-only failures”).

Dylan Brooks: Customer list: do we have names? I’ve heard Sales has at least one healthcare-ish prospect asking for safe model upgrade tooling.

Marissa Cole: Sales has 3 in pipeline; I’ll keep them anonymized here:
- Enterprise A (healthcare ISV) – wants to test model upgrade w/out risk
- Enterprise B (fintech) – cares about audit logs + retention controls
- Mid-market C (support automation SaaS) – cares about latency/cost

Marissa Cole: For beta, I’m thinking we pick 2 that are most “cooperative” + have clear evaluation tasks.

Naomi Feldman: Fintech one will likely ask about data residency early. Can we constrain beta to US regions only until we confirm residency controls?

Logan Wright: Telemetry pipelines also simpler if we do US-only first. Less partitioning complexity.

Paula Mendes: Works for me. Beta: US-only, allowlist required.

Talia Benson: I’ll capture as a decision: Beta is US regions only + org allowlist required + opt-in.

Marissa Cole: Open question: how much sampling % do we allow in beta by default? I want safe defaults.

Logan Wright: Suggest hard cap per route (e.g., max 1%) and global cap per org. Let SRE tune based on capacity.

Chloe Martin: And backend should reject configs that exceed cap (not “best effort”). Avoid accidental GPU spike.

Naomi Feldman: Also cap impacts data volume/retention cost, so good.

Dylan Brooks: UI can show “requested sampling” vs “effective sampling” if caps clamp it.

Marissa Cole: GA criteria updates based on this thread:
- Beta: single shadow target per route; dashboards + alerting; gates visible but not enforced
- Beta: US regions only, org allowlist + explicit opt-in
- Beta: sampling defaults low (<=0.5%? capped at 1%); enforced server-side
- Security: redaction on by default; retention default 7 days; configurable to 0; restricted access
- Telemetry: stable dims + separate dropped vs error metrics

Marissa Cole: Anything else we should put as “must-have for beta”?

Paula Mendes: Need a one-click kill switch in Console admin (global + per-route), no deploy.

Dylan Brooks: Already in plan. We’ll add it to beta checklist explicitly.

Naomi Feldman: + audit log entry when someone changes shadow sampling / retention / redaction settings.

Logan Wright: That’s actually helpful for debugging too. (who changed config?)

Chloe Martin: If we add audit logs, we should confirm where they live (existing control-plane audit stream). Should be doable.

Talia Benson: Action items:
- Marissa: update PRD/beta plan w decisions + send to stakeholders
- Paula: define beta “read-only gate” UX + what thresholds we recommend (if any)
- Logan: propose final metric dimensions + caps; share with Dylan/Chloe
- Naomi: draft customer-facing language for opt-in + retention/redaction defaults

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: I’ll post PRD update end of day and schedule a 30m check-in tomorrow with Console/Telemetry/Security to confirm we’re aligned on defaults + customer messaging.
